theater: 山西雁門郡靈丘與平型關道

battle.name: 翟松柏起義
battle.theater: 山西雁門郡靈丘與平型關道
battle.brief: 大業十二年（616年）正月初七，雁門郡人翟松柏於靈丘聚眾數萬，轉攻鄰近各縣，是隋末北方邊郡規模罕見的起事。卡面這件秦連弩正是關隘守軍用來壓住攻勢的兵器：弩機儲力、一踩一發，連續射擊把進攻隊形釘在牆外。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的兩方是隋朝與以翟松柏為首的雁門起義軍。隋朝此時疆域東極於海、西抵西域，是東亞最盛的國家，但開皇年間的軍制已在大業朝消耗殆盡。軍權分兩層：中央尚書省兵部掌符節與軍令，前線設行軍總管、總管、判官，郡縣由太守、令率郡兵應敵，邊郡另置屯田戍卒與烽燧亭障。大業十一年雁門被突厥圍困時，朝廷下詔天下諸郡募兵，守令競來赴難，募兵與郡兵混編自此成為主力，府兵編制則名存實亡。起義軍一方，領袖只有翟松柏一人，沒有可考的幕僚與將領體系，所部是聚在鄉里的農民、逃戶與市井散兵，多無甲胄而多有耕獵器具改成的兵器。起義中心在雁門郡靈丘，郡治雁門縣即今山西代縣，郡下領雁門、靈丘、繁畤、五台、崞五縣，靈丘在郡域東南的太行北口，是塞內農耕區與塞外牧地的交會處。北方還有別的武裝與這場起事並肩而行：前一年三月魏刀兒自號歷山飛，眾各十餘萬，北連突厥；翌年四月其部將甄翟兒亦號歷山飛，眾十萬，轉寇太原；同年八月賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬自恆山寇高陽。這些人馬同樣出自大業年間的流民與逃戶，說明亂事已不是單一郡縣的治安問題，而是整條北方邊線的崩解。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the Sui dynasty and the Yanmen rebel army led by Zhai Songbai. At this point Sui's territory reached the sea in the east and the western regions in the west, and it was the wealthiest state in East Asia, but the military system built in the Kaihuang era had been spent almost to nothing during the Daye reign. Command was layered in two tiers: at the centre the Ministry of War under the Department of State Affairs held the tallies and the written orders, and the field army had travelling army commissioners, commandants and registrars, while prefects of commanderies and magistrates of counties led commandery troops, and the frontier commanderies additionally maintained garrison settlers, beacon towers and barrier forts. When Yanmen was besieged by the Turks in Daye 11, the court ordered the commanderies of the realm to raise volunteers, and the local officers vied with each other to come to the rescue; from that point on units mixing hired soldiers with commandery troops became the main force, while the fubing establishment existed in name only. On the rebel side the leadership consisted of Zhai Songbai alone, with no recorded staff and no general structure; his men were peasants, deserters and loose men from the towns who had gathered in the villages, mostly without armour and mostly carrying farm and hunting tools converted into weapons. The centre of the rising was Lingqiu in Yanmen commandery, whose seat, Yanmen county, is today's Dai County in Shanxi; the commandery administered five counties, Yanmen, Lingqiu, Fanshi, Wutai and Gao, and Lingqiu lay to the southeast of the commandery at the northern mouth of the Taihang range, where the farming zone inside the passes met the pasture land beyond them. Other armed bands moved on the same northern front as this rising: in the third month of the year before, Wei Dao’er styled himself Lishanfei and drew a following of more than a hundred thousand, joining hands with the Turks; in the fourth month of the next year his subordinate Zhen Zhai’er also took the title Lishanfei, gathered a hundred thousand men and turned on Taiyuan; and in the eighth month of that same year the rebel leader Zhao Wanhai led several tens of thousands out of Hengshan against Gaoyang. These were also deserters and refugees from the Daye years, which shows that the trouble was no longer a policing matter in one commandery but the collapse of an entire northern frontier line.
people: 翟松柏，雁門郡人，生卒與出身都不見於史傳。《隋書》卷四《帝紀第四》與《北史》卷十二《隋本紀下》為他留下的全部文字只有一句：十二年春正月甲午，雁門人翟松柏起兵於靈丘，眾至數萬，轉攻傍縣。他與瓦崗的翟讓、東郡韋城人，年代相近而地望懸殊，名字又只差一字，後世常把兩人混為一談；而與北面的歷山飛部將甄翟兒更是毫無關係的另一支人馬。真正決定他命運的大人物在洛陽與江都。隋煬帝楊廣自604年即位，616年正月起兵的時候人在東都洛陽；同年秋七月甲子正式幸江都宮，以越王侗與段達、元文都、韋津、盧楚等總留守後事。勸阻巡幸的奉信郎崔民象在建國門上表，被解其頤後斬之；再諫請還西京的王愛仁也被殺。前一年雁門被圍之役，決定死守的是民部尚書樊子蓋，他力主據堅城以挫其銳、坐徵四方兵使入援，與主張輕騎突圍的宇文述相持不下；樊子蓋在大業十二年七月壬戌卒，翟松柏起兵後不到半年，主張死守邊城的那位重臣就死了。屯衛將軍雲定興奉詔募兵，十六歲的李世民隸其麾下，獻策多繼旗鼓為疑兵，虜騎因此疑有重兵而不敢盡力攻。另一端的隋將張須陀同年被瓦崗翟讓、李密擊敗，最精銳的一支騎兵被吸在河南；將軍潘長文討歷山飛部將甄翟兒，反為所敗而死。
peopleEn: Zhai Songbai was a man of Yanmen commandery, and neither his dates nor his background appear in any surviving biography. The Book of Sui, juan four, Annals of Emperor Yang, and the Bei Shi, juan twelve, Sui annals, give him in total one sentence: in the first month of the spring of the twelfth year of Daye, on the jiawu day, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen raised troops at Lingqiu, gathered tens of thousands of men, and turned on the neighbouring counties. He had nothing in common with Zhai Rang of the Wagang band, who was from Weicheng in Dong commandery, though their names differ by a single character and later writers constantly merged the two; he was equally unrelated to the Northern leader Zhen Zhai’er, who served under Lishanfei. The men who actually decided his fate were in Luoyang and Jiangdu. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, had taken the throne in 604, and when the rising began in the first month of 616 he was at the eastern capital of Luoyang; in the seventh month of the same year, on the jiazi day, he formally moved to the Jiangdu palace, leaving the prince Yue Tong together with Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin, Lu Chu and others to hold the capital in his stead. Cui Minxiang, a courier-official, presented a memorial at the Jianguo Gate warning against the tour and had his jaw broken before being beheaded; Wang Airen, who then urged the emperor to return to the western capital, was killed as well. In the siege of Yanmen the year before, the man who insisted on holding the city was the Minister of Revenue Fan Zigao, who argued for using the fortified city to blunt the enemy’s edge and waiting for the armies of the four quarters to come in, and who opposed the plan to break out with a few thousand light cavalry; Fan Zigao died on the renxu day of the seventh month of Daye 12, less than half a year after the rising began. The garrison commander Yun Dingxing had been ordered to raise volunteers for the relief of Yanmen, and the sixteen-year-old Li Shimin, serving under him, proposed that they keep sending up banners and drums in sequence so as to feign the arrival of relief armies, a ruse that made the Turks doubt the strength of the besieged city and hesitate to press the attack. On the other front the Sui general Zhang Xuetuo was defeated in the same year by Zhai Rang and Li Mi of the Wagang band, so the finest cavalry in the empire was drawn away into Henan; the general Pan Changwen, sent against Zhen Zhai’er of the Lishanfei band, was defeated and died.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩屬於年代卡：它確是這個戰場上該有的兵器，但《隋書》本紀完全沒有記錄雙方配發了哪些弩機，實際部署只能從器械原理與地勢推想。秦時已有成熟的弩機，歷來出土的秦墓弩機、秦簡所記的弩法，可以看出弓弩在秦軍中的份量；東漢馬援又改進為可連發的連弩，傳世記載稱其一發十矢，魏晉南北朝各代沿用不輟，到隋代仍是城頭與隘口的常備器械。連弩的機械原理正是卡面那句話：弩機把拉力存起來，上弦一次便可踩機連發，不必每次重拉弓弦，射速遠高於單發的臂弩，代價是弩機結構細密、沙泥入機難以復原、儲好的力一旦被撞斷便全無用處，射程與破甲力也遠不及大弩床弩。放到616年的雁門線上，它的價值恰好落在最需要的地方：靈丘與平型關之間是太行北段的狹窄谷道，騎兵難以展開，雲梯、撞車這類攻城器械在碎石坡上難以運作，守方居高臨下用連續的弩雨壓住密集的進攻隊形，一踩一發的射速意味著短時間內能傾瀉大量箭矢，把衝鋒的人釘在牆外。與它配套的還有床弩與弓手、投石機、壕塹與拒馬，以及沿塞垣傳遞警號的烽燧亭障。起義軍一側的裝備就樸素得多：絕大多數人只有削尖的木杆長矛、環首刀、耙叉與漁叉，皮甲布甲極少，完全沒有攻城器械，糧食靠田間搶收與村寨徵集，運輸靠畜力與步力沿滹沱河谷北運，馬匹奇缺，所以一旦離開山地就再也追不上官軍。
kitsEn: The repeating crossbow on the card is an anachronism card, and it is a piece that genuinely belonged on this battlefield, but the annals of the Book of Sui record nothing whatever about which crossbow locks either side was issued, so the actual deployment can only be inferred from the mechanics of the weapon and from the terrain. Mature crossbow locks already existed in the Qin period, and the crossbow locks excavated from Qin tombs together with the crossbow ordinances in the Qin bamboo slips show how large a share of the Qin army archery held; in Eastern Han times Ma Yuan improved the type into the repeating crossbow, transmitted accounts describing it as loosing ten bolts at a stroke, and the Wei, Jin and the northern and southern dynasties carried it on without interruption, so that in the Sui it remained a standard piece of equipment on the wall and at the pass. The mechanical principle is exactly the sentence on the card: the lock stores the draw, so the bow is cocked once and then fired repeatedly by treading the trigger, and the rate of fire is far above that of a single-shot hand crossbow; the price is that the lock is finely made, that once sand or mud works into it the mechanism is hard to restore, and that if the stored tension is broken by a blow the piece is useless, while its range and armour-piercing power fall far short of the great bed crossbows. On the Yanmen line of 616 its value fell exactly where it was needed: between Lingqiu and Pingxing Pass lie the narrow valleys of the northern Taihang range, cavalry cannot deploy there, and engines such as scaling ladders and battering rams are hard to haul over a scree slope, while the defenders looking down from the heights met the dense attacking formation with a continuous rain of bolts; the speed of the tread-launched repeating crossbow meant a great many arrows could be poured out in a short time, pinning the charging men outside the wall. Working with it were the bed crossbows and the archers, the stone-throwers, the trenches and the spiked barricades, and the beacon towers and barrier forts that passed the alarm along the line of the frontier fortification. The rebels' equipment was far plainer: the great majority had only sharpened wooden-shaft spears, ring-pommel sabres, pitchforks and fishing spears, hide and cloth armour were very scarce, they had no siege engines at all, they lived off what they took from the fields and gathered from the villages, their supplies moved north by pack animals and porters along the Hutuo valley, and they had almost no horses, which is why once they left the hills they could never catch up with the Sui columns.
tactics: 起義軍的打法是鄉民起事的典型：以靈丘縣城為核心，先集結後散開，移動與再集結都靠鄉里網絡和熟悉地形的山民嚮導。起兵初期人數直上數萬，走的是流動打擊而非固守，一路轉攻鄰近各縣，切斷郡治與汾晉平原之間的糧道。隊伍多帶三日乾糧，遇到城池多數只作圍擾與襲取而不強攻，因為他們既沒有攻城器械，也沒有攻城的技術，這正是連弩這類守城武器能派上用場的前提。缺少馬匹使他們難以快速傳令和追擊，一旦離開山地進入平原，與官軍主力接觸，人數與陣形都難維持。隋軍一側以郡兵與募兵混編的隊伍為主，自雁門關與太原晉陽兩個方向合進，沿官道與山谷路南下，分為前鋒、弩手隊與預備隊；據城禦守時以城頭弩陣壓制，野戰時用騎兵兩翼包抄。對付流動起義的標準辦法是圍城與斷糧：先切斷靈丘與鄉村之間的運糧小徑，再四面合圍收緊，逼起義軍在缺糧乏彈時出來決戰，而連弩正是在城頭與隘口反覆使用的器械，射速快而射擊連續，足以在官軍尚未合圍之前先把進攻方的前鋒壓退。值得警惕的是前一年雁門之役的結局：突厥騎兵攻入雁門郡四十一城中的三十九城，只有雁門與崞兩城未下，說明北方城防的實際狀況；同年四月，歷山飛部將甄翟兒眾十萬轉寇太原，將軍潘長文討之反為所敗而死，隋軍在北方已無可恃的統帥與主力。雙方具體的進攻次序、陣形編組與傷亡數字，正史都沒有留下記載，只能從制度與地勢去推想。
tacticsEn: The way the rebels fought was that of a typical rising of village armed men: the county seat of Lingqiu was the core, and they first concentrated and then dispersed, moving and meeting again through the network of village ties and through local guides who knew the ground. In the first days the numbers swelled straight to tens of thousands, and what they practised was mobile striking rather than holding ground; they turned on the neighbouring counties one after another, cutting the grain road between the commandery seat and the Fen and Jin plains. The bands carried about three days of dry rations, and when they met a walled town they surrounded it, harassed it and struck by surprise rather than delivering a real assault, because they had neither siege engines nor the technique to use them, and that is precisely the condition that gives a defending crossbow its part to play. Having very few horses they could not pass orders quickly or pursue, and once they left the hills and came into contact with the main body of the Sui army on the plain they could hold neither their numbers nor their formation. The Sui army, on the other hand, worked from units mixing commandery soldiers with volunteers, advancing on two axes from Yanmen Pass and from the Jinyang area of Taiyuan, moving south along the official roads and the valley tracks, and dividing into vanguard, crossbow companies and a reserve. When they sat in a walled town they used the crossbow line on the wall to bear down on the attackers; in the field they used cavalry on both wings to envelop. The standard answer to a mobile rising was to besiege and to cut supplies: sever the small grain paths between Lingqiu and the villages, then tighten the noose from four sides, forcing the rebels out to fight when they had neither provisions nor ammunition left; and the repeating crossbow was exactly the piece used again and again from the wall and the pass, fast in rate of fire and continuous in shooting, more than enough to push back the attackers’ vanguard before the Sui columns had even closed. What should give pause is the outcome of the siege of Yanmen the year before: the Turk cavalry entered thirty-nine of the forty-one cities of Yanmen commandery, and only Yanmen and Gao did not fall, which shows the true condition of northern city defence. In the fourth month of the same year Zhen Zhai’er of the Lishanfei band turned on Taiyuan with a hundred thousand men, and the general Pan Changwen sent against him was defeated and died; the Sui had by then no dependable commander and no dependable main force in the north. The actual order of attack on both sides, the grouping of formations and the casualty figures are not preserved in the official histories, and can only be inferred from the institutions and the ground.
data: 有據可查的數字不多，逐一列出。時間：大業十二年正月初七甲午日，即616年農曆正月初七，翟松柏於靈丘起兵。兵力：正史記眾至數萬，這是唯一的兵數記載，數萬之眾是概數，無法拆分步騎，也無法分派到各縣。行政：起兵地雁門郡下轄五縣，郡治雁門縣在今山西代縣，靈丘、五台、崞、繁畤分列東南。距離：靈丘縣城到平型關約四十公里，到五台縣城約七十公里，到繁畤約八十公里，到崞縣即今原平崞陽一帶約一百五十公里，到郡治雁門縣約一百四十公里，到太原晉陽約二百五十公里。前一年雁門之圍可作對照：突厥騎兵攻入雁門郡四十一城中的三十九城，唯雁門與崞不下，圍城之中兵民十五萬口、存食僅可支二旬，朝廷下詔天下諸郡募兵救援，至九月甲辰始解圍而去。同一年的北方數字：四月魏刀兒所部將甄翟兒號歷山飛，眾十萬，轉寇太原，隋將潘長文討之反為所敗而死；八月賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬自恆山寇高陽；十月宇文述薨；十二月唐公李淵破甄翟兒於西河，《資治通鑑》卷百八十三同繫於大業十二年，載其戰於雀鼠谷；至於洛口倉與李密自號魏公，《隋書》本紀繫於大業十三年二月，《資治通鑑》則繫於大業十二年，兩書相差一年。靈丘與平型關一線的谷道狹窄，冬季積雪封山，限制騎兵與車兵的展開速度。關於翟松柏本人，正史只留下起兵日期與眾數，起義之後的出兵討平之師、將領姓名、交戰地點、斬獲與亡失數目，兩部史書都沒有記載，連編纂較晚、收事更細的《資治通鑑》在大業十二年一卷中，也沒有為他立傳。
dataEn: The figures that can actually be vouched for are few, and they are set out one by one. Date: the jiawu day of the seventh day of the first month of Daye 12, that is the seventh day of the first lunar month of 616, when Zhai Songbai raised his troops at Lingqiu. Numbers: the official histories record that he gathered tens of thousands of men; this is the only troop figure preserved, it is a round number, and it cannot be broken down into foot and horse or apportioned among the counties. Administration: the commandery in which the rising began, Yanmen, administered five counties; its seat, Yanmen county, lies in today’s Dai County, Shanxi, while Lingqiu, Wutai, Gao and Fanshi lay off to the southeast. Distances: from the county seat of Lingqiu about forty kilometres to Pingxing Pass, about seventy to the seat of Wutai county, about eighty to Fanshi, about a hundred and fifty to Gao county in today’s Yuanping at Huoyang, about a hundred and forty to the commandery seat of Yanmen county, and about two hundred and fifty to Jinyang in Taiyuan. The siege of Yanmen the year before provides a comparison: the Turk cavalry entered thirty-nine of the forty-one cities of Yanmen commandery, and only Yanmen and Gao did not fall; inside the besieged city were a hundred and fifty thousand soldiers and people with stores of food good for only twenty days; the court ordered the commanderies of the realm to raise volunteers to relieve it, and the siege was not lifted until the jiachen day of the ninth month. The northern figures of the same year: in the fourth month Zhen Zhai’er, the subordinate of Wei Dao’er, took the title Lishanfei, gathered a hundred thousand men and turned on Taiyuan, and the Sui general Pan Changwen sent against him was defeated and died; in the eighth month the rebel leader Zhao Wanhai led several tens of thousands out of Hengshan against Gaoyang; in the tenth month Yuwen Shu died; in the twelfth month Li Yuan of Tang defeated Zhen Zhai’er in the western reaches of the Fen, the Comprehensive Mirror placing the same year and recording the engagement at Queqin Valley. As for the capture of the Luokou granary and Li Mi’s assumption of the title Duke of Wei, the annals of the Book of Sui place it in the second month of Daye 13, while the Comprehensive Mirror places it in Daye 12, a difference of a full year between the two authorities. The valley road along the Lingqiu and Pingxing route is narrow, and in winter the passes close under snow, restricting how fast cavalry and wagon trains can deploy. As for Zhai Songbai himself, the official histories preserve only the date of the rising and the size of the crowd; the column sent to put it down, the name of its commander, the place where they fought, and the numbers taken or lost are recorded in neither history, and even the later and far more detailed Comprehensive Mirror, in its volume for the twelfth year of Daye, did not enter him into the record at all.
cause: 導火線是616年正月初七靈丘的聚眾，根子卻在三徵高句麗之後國力的急劇透支。開皇年間留下的府兵與糧倉體系本足以支撐一次大規模邊防行動，大業朝卻把它們連年透支：西征吐谷渾、再征高句麗，每次都徵發大批丁壯，河北山東的民戶被拉走，逃戶成為常態，府庫空虛而郡縣吏望風沮敗，士民疲於役使。邊郡的處境更壞，靈丘、繁畤一線既要供應邊軍的軍糧與轉輸，又要承受州縣額外的攤派，戶口大量流散，鄉里之間的互助與衝突都到了臨界點。前一年的雁門之圍把這一點推到明面：突厥圍城，郡中四十一城失其三十九，官軍頻戰不利，朝廷靠下詔天下募兵才勉強守住雁門與崞兩城，圍解之後又曲赦太原、雁門郡死罪已下。募兵制度把大批無籍流民編入軍中，當然解了燃眉之急，卻同時在雁門一線造出一群有武裝而無歸屬的人；死罪赦免又使亡命之徒無所顧忌，亂的種子就埋在這一年。隋廷自己的判斷也說明危機已經全面：同年七月煬帝巡幸江都，群臣崔民象、王愛仁先後以盜賊充斥力諫，一死一斬，而首都留守只留段達、元文都、韋津、盧楚數人鎮守洛陽，北方邊事再無得力之人。民間層面另有推力：通鑑所記李密語，謂人人皆云楊氏將滅、李氏將興，又以劉、項起於布衣終為帝王相激勵，讖語與歌謠在河南、河北、山西一帶流傳，百姓把兵亂、災荒與讖語連在一起解讀，起兵者只要打起旗號，響應的人就會很快聚集。地方上豪族與遊俠的武裝傳統同樣存在，晉北、雁門一線民間多有私兵與獵戶，山道、糧倉與城守一旦失守，官府對鄉里的控制就會迅速崩解。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the gathering of men at Lingqiu on the seventh day of the first month of 616, but the root lay in the Sui state whose strength had been catastrophically overdrawn by the campaigns against Goguryeo. The fubing system and the storehouses of the Kaihuang era had been sufficient to sustain a single large frontier operation, but the Daye reign drew on them year after year: the western expedition against Tuyuhun, then the campaigns against Goguryeo, each time dragging away great numbers of labouring men, emptying the households of Hebei and Shandong, making flight a permanent feature of life, and leaving the treasuries bare while the local officers broke at the first sign of the enemy and the people were worn out by service. The situation of the frontier commanderies was worse still: the Lingqiu and Fanshi line had to supply the grain and the transport of the frontier army while also bearing additional levies from the prefectures, the population was scattered widely, and both the mutual aid and the friction of village society had reached a breaking point. The siege of Yanmen the year before pushed this to the surface: the Turks besieged the city, the court lost thirty-nine of the forty-one cities of the commandery, the Sui troops fought badly and repeatedly, and only the arrival of volunteers raised throughout the realm allowed Yanmen and Gao to be held at all; after the siege was lifted the court further pardoned all those under sentence of death in the Taiyuan and Yanmen commanderies. The recruiting system threw large numbers of men without household registration into the army, which answered the emergency of the moment, but it simultaneously manufactured in the Yanmen area a population that was armed and belonged to no one; the pardon in turn left fugitives from the law with nothing to fear, and the seed of the disorder was planted in that year. The court’s own judgement shows that the crisis had become general: in the seventh month of the same year the emperor went on tour to Jiangdu, and the courtiers Cui Minxiang and Wang Airen petitioned in turn that the empire was swamped with bandits; one was beheaded and the other killed, while at the capital only a handful of men — Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin and Lu Chu — were left to hold Luoyang, and the northern frontier was given no competent man. At the level of popular belief there was a further push. The Comprehensive Mirror records Li Mi telling his hearers that everyone was saying the Yang house would perish and the Li house would rise, and he urged them on with the precedent of Liu Bang and Xiang Yu, who both began as commoners and ended as emperors; prophecies and songs circulated through Henan, Hebei and Shanxi, and the common people read rebellion, famine and prophecy together, so that once a rebel raised a banner the response came quickly. The armed tradition of local great families and wandering swordsmen mattered as well: in northern Shanxi and along the Yanmen line there were private bands and hunters, and once the positions that mattered for the mountain roads, the granaries and the defence of the towns fell, the government’s hold over the countryside broke down at once.
impact: 就眼前的軍局而言，這場起義的規模有限，而且正史只記起兵與轉攻鄰縣一句，連平定或覆滅的過程都沒有留下，因此它的直接結果只能從旁證推想。可以確定的是它發生在隋朝北方防線最脆弱的時候：616年正月翟松柏起兵，四月歷山飛部將甄翟兒眾十萬轉寇太原、隋將潘長文敗死，同年八月賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬自恆山寇高陽；翌年正月竇建德在河間樂壽設壇自稱長樂王，杜伏威渡淮攻陷歷陽，二月劉武周在馬邑殺太守王仁恭舉兵、北連突厥；河南一線則是李密與翟讓攻取洛口倉、眾至數十萬，李密自號魏公，河南諸郡相繼皆陷。一年之內的起事密度，說明隋廷對地方的控制在616至617年已只剩一層薄殼；翟松柏在靈丘點火，與太原、馬邑、河北、江淮的起義屬於同一場全面崩解的開端。另一層影響在地理上：雁門與代北是關內通往塞北的孔道，隋廷把主要兵力調去河南與山東，北線空虛，隨即被李淵集團與劉武周利用。同一年的十二月，朝廷以右驍衛大將軍唐公李淵為太原留守，討歷山飛部將甄翟兒，戰於雀鼠谷，李世民率精兵自萬軍之中救出其父李淵，正是這支新軍第一次壓制北面的戰役；翌年李淵西征、太原兵力抽空之際，劉武周自馬邑起兵後乘虛攻取晉陽、太原，北方形勢再度崩解。從長線看，隋末群雄的割據幾乎都沿著同一條邏輯：據險、聚眾、徵糧、而後取郡縣，翟松柏在靈丘做的正是這一套的第一步，只是他沒有走到後面。最後是記憶的層面：翟松柏的名字在傳世文獻裡只留下兩三行，後人往往把他與瓦崗的翟讓混為一人，連雁門起義與瓦崗軍也常被並在一起講，一場改變了山西北部十年間走向的邊亂，幾乎從歷史敘述裡消失。
impactEn: As far as the immediate military situation was concerned, the rising was of limited scale, and since the official histories record only the rising itself and the turning on the neighbouring counties, without even the process of its suppression or its destruction, its immediate outcome can only be inferred from the evidence alongside it. What can be established is that it happened when the Sui’s northern defensive line was at its weakest: the rising began in the first month of 616; in the fourth month Zhen Zhai’er of the Lishanfei band turned on Taiyuan with a hundred thousand men and the Sui general Pan Changwen fell in defeat; in the eighth month of the same year Zhao Wanhai led several tens of thousands out of Hengshan against Gaoyang; in the first month of the year after Dou Jiande set up his altar at Leshou in Hebei and proclaimed himself Prince of Changle, and Du Fuwei crossed the Huai and seized Liyang, while in the second month Liu Wuzhou, the commandant of Mayi, killed the governor Wang Rengong, raised troops and drew the Turks to his side; in Henan it was Li Mi and Zhai Rang who took the Luokou granary, Li Mi proclaimed himself Duke of Wei with a following of several tens of thousands, and the commanderies of Henan fell one after another. A density of risings such as this within a single year shows that the court’s control over the localities had by 616 and 617 been reduced to a thin shell; Zhai Songbai’s fire at Lingqiu belonged to the same opening of a general collapse as the risings at Taiyuan, Mayi, in Hebei and along the Jiang and Huai. There is a second layer of consequence, and it is geographic. Yanmen and northern Dai were the corridor by which the interior of the empire connected with the steppe, and with the main body of troops drawn away to Henan and Shandong, the northern line was left hollow and was promptly used by Li Yuan’s group and by Liu Wuzhou. In December of that same year the court appointed the Duke of Tang, Li Yuan, as governor of Taiyuan and sent him against Zhen Zhai’er of the Lishanfei band; the fight at Queqin Valley followed, and Li Shimin led elite troops out of a ring of tens of thousands to rescue his own father Li Yuan, marking the first time this new army bore down successfully on the northern front. In the year after, when Li Yuan campaigned west and the garrison of Taiyuan was drawn off, Liu Wuzhou, having risen at Mayi, took advantage of the opening to seize Jinyang and Taiyuan, and the northern situation collapsed a second time. Seen along the longer arc, nearly every regime that carved up the late Sui followed the same logic: hold the difficult ground, gather men, levy grain, and only then take the commanderies and counties — and what Zhai Songbai did at Lingqiu was the first step of exactly that sequence, except that he never got past the first step. Last there is the layer of memory. The name of Zhai Songbai survives in the transmitted literature in two or three lines only; later writers constantly merge him with Zhai Rang of the Wagang band, and even the Yanmen rising and the Wagang army are often told as one and the same business, so that a frontier rising which changed the course of northern Shanxi for a decade very nearly disappeared from the historical narrative.
result: 結果一節最需要說清楚的，是正史對這場起義的記載有多稀薄。《隋書》卷四《帝紀第四·煬帝下》與《北史》卷十二《隋本紀下》為翟松柏留下的全部文字是同一句：十二年春正月甲午，雁門人翟松柏起兵於靈丘，眾至數萬，轉攻傍縣。兩部史書都沒有寫他何時被平、是否被平、由誰領兵討平；《資治通鑑》編到大業十二年一卷，也未收此條，該卷記載的翟氏是東郡韋城的翟讓與歷山飛部下的甄翟兒，與靈丘的翟松柏無涉。因此可以確定的結果有四項。其一，起義確實發生並且一度成規模，數萬之眾在正月初七集結於靈丘，隨即轉攻鄰近各縣，這是616年北方邊郡規模罕見的起事，而且《隋書》在大業十二年正月就把它記了出來，說明朝廷在當年就知曉了此事。其二，隋廷對此的處置在史書上沒有留下痕跡，既不見下令討平的詔令，也不見記載出兵的統帥，與同年被明確記錄的張子路、操天成、李軌等較小規模的起義相比，翟松柏反而更為沉寂，這本身就是北方秩序失控的證據。其三，他沒有在隋末形成割據一方，也沒有像魏刀兒、歷山飛、甄翟兒那樣留下可以追索的部眾與地名，隋亡時北方已盡為竇建德、劉武周、李密所分，也沒有他的名字出現其中；他在史書上唯一留下的痕跡，就是那一句起兵記錄。其四，記載雖然簡陋，起義的意義仍然清楚：到616年，隋朝在雁門、代北這樣的重鎮與邊郡，已經能夠在一夜之間聚起數萬之眾，而這樣的起義在一年之內可以出現很多次，每一次都要用兵役去平，每一次都讓中央更虛弱，最終兩年後隋室覆亡。
resultEn: What most needs setting out in this section is how thin the official record of this rising is. The Book of Sui, juan four, Annals of Emperor Yang, lower part, and the Bei Shi, juan twelve, Sui annals, give Zhai Songbai the same single sentence: in the first month of the spring of the twelfth year of Daye, on the jiawu day, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen raised troops at Lingqiu, gathered tens of thousands of men, and turned on the neighbouring counties. Neither history records when he was put down, whether he was put down, or who led the troops that dealt with him; the Comprehensive Mirror, in its volume for the twelfth year of Daye, does not take him up either, and the two Zhai of that volume are Zhai Rang of Weicheng in Dong commandery and Zhen Zhai’er of the Lishanfei band, neither of whom has anything to do with Zhai Songbai of Lingqiu. Four outcomes can therefore be stated with certainty. First, the rising certainly happened and certainly reached a scale: tens of thousands gathered at Lingqiu on the seventh day of the first month and immediately turned on the neighbouring counties, making it one of the largest risings in the northern frontier commanderies of 616, and the fact that the Book of Sui enters it in the very first month of Daye 12 shows the court knew of it at the time. Second, the handling of it by the Sui leaves no trace in the histories: there is neither an edict ordering it suppressed nor any record of a commander sent out, and compared with the smaller risings of Zhang Zilu, Cao Tiancheng and Li Gui, which are plainly recorded in the same year, Zhai Songbai is markedly more obscure, and that obscurity is itself evidence that the northern order had slipped out of control. Third, he never formed a power of his own in the late Sui, and left behind neither a following nor a place-name that can be traced, in the way Wei Dao’er, Lishanfei and Zhen Zhai’er did; by the time the Sui fell the north had been divided entirely among Dou Jiande, Liu Wuzhou and Li Mi, and his name does not appear among them; the single trace he leaves in the historical record is that one sentence about his rising. Fourth, though the record is thin, the meaning of the rising is clear: by 616 the Sui, in strongholds and frontier commanderies such as Yanmen and northern Dai, could already raise tens of thousands of men in the space of a single night, and such risings could occur many times within a year, each of them requiring levies to put down, and each of them leaving the centre weaker, until two years later the Sui house fell.
